1.explanation: These files cover the core logic and tests that detect CPU idle periods and calculate Time to Interactive (and related metrics) both in direct DevTools traces and in Lantern’s simulated environment. “first-cpu-idle” and “interactive” tests exercise the algorithms that throw NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD when no quiet window is found. The Lantern variants, plus the load simulator and trace-parsing tests, ensure we understand how traces are processed and how simulated CPU throttling impacts TTI/TBT. Reviewing and modifying these will be key to reproducing and fixing the missing idle-period error.
1.bug_scenario: In the provided screenshot of the Lighthouse Performance panel, First Contentful Paint, Speed Index, and Largest Contentful Paint are successfully measured (green). However, Time to Interactive and Total Blocking Time both fail and display “Error!” with the code NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD. This occurs when DevTools is set to “provided throttling,” and the page deliberately delays FCP (via a query-param) but then sits idle immediately afterward—so Lighthouse never finds a sufficiently long quiet period on the main thread to compute TTI or TBT.
